body:
It is unclear to me what happens in Chrome if the inform-the-navigation-api-about-aborting-navigation which is triggered from the second pushState triggers third pushState call via navigateerror event listener. Stack then unwinds an continues executing, but in which state are we in then? Edit: Chrome's renderer process crashes

@noamr

I believe the divergence between chromium and the spec is that chromium runs [#set-the-ongoing-navigation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#set-the-ongoing-navigation) as part of the [#inner-navigate-event-firing-algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#inner-navigate-event-firing-algorithm). According to a [TODO I left myself](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/3143697c/third_party/blink/renderer/core/navigation_api/navigation_api.cc#723), the spec is right and chromium is wrong.

I think what's missing in the spec is that [#set-the-ongoing-navigation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#set-the-ongoing-navigation) should be included in [#shared-history-push/replace-state-steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#shared-history-push/replace-state-steps)?

> It is unclear to me what happens in Chrome if the inform-the-navigation-api-about-aborting-navigation which is triggered from the second pushState triggers third pushState call via navigateerror event listener. Stack then unwinds an continues executing, but in which state are we in then? Edit: Chrome's renderer process crashes

I think this is only possible because `navigateerror` is fired synchronously inside [#abort-the-ongoing-navigation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#abort-the-ongoing-navigation)? So we could fire `navigateerror` on a microtask instead, or early-exit somewhere (probably in [#inner-navigate-event-firing-algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#inner-navigate-event-firing-algorithm)) if [the ongoing navigate event](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#ongoing-navigate-event) is not null? I'd lean toward the early-exit, since changing `navigateerror` timing all but guarantees that the `navigateerror` will fire after the next `navigate`.

Nice catch. The root cause here is that the navigation API's notion of "ongoing navigation" is always async (i.e., it takes at least until a microtask checkpoint for the `finished` promise to settle). Whereas, `pushState()` is completely sync. Mostly this mismatch is OK, but in the case of overlapping navigations and transitions we can get into trouble

For this reason, @natechapin's suggestion.

> I think what's missing in the spec is that [#set-the-ongoing-navigation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#set-the-ongoing-navigation) should be included in [#shared-history-push/replace-state-steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#shared-history-push/replace-state-steps)?

doesn't quite work. Per https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/6927#issuecomment-987747199 , to match browsers, we want the results for

```js
location.href = "foo.html";
history.pushState(1, null, "#1");
```

to be a navigation to `#1` and then a navigation to `foo.html`. (This is the "XDN then SDN" case.) The way the spec currently accomplishes this is by having `history.pushState()` not touch the "ongoing navigation" machinery at all.

If we implemented Nate's suggestion, then step 21.2 of the [navigate](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#navigate) algorithm for `foo.html` would notice that the ongoing navigation has changed, and abort the navigation to `foo.html`. (Which sounds like pretty sensible behavior to me! But is not at all what browsers do, so, oh well.)

---

The fix @farre mentions

> Looking at Chromium source, we see that [#inform-the-navigation-api-about-aborting-navigation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#inform-the-navigation-api-about-aborting-navigation) is called in [NavigationApi::DispatchNavigateEvent](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/core/navigation_api/navigation_api.cc;l=728;drc=87fedd04f34e479b4d5a45f957f09b79d45e3cee), and indeed if I add a call to [#inform-the-navigation-api-about-aborting-navigation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#inform-the-navigation-api-about-aborting-navigation) in Gecko's implementation of [#inner-navigate-event-firing-algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#inner-navigate-event-firing-algorithm) the assert obviously stops being a problem.

is one reasonable way of patching over the inconsistency. It basically says "for the purposes of the navigation API and its promises and events, let's abort the ongoing navigation". (Whereas for the purposes of the rest of the navigation stack, we don't abort.) Although, it sounds like we need some further patches to avoid a crash.

I think this direction is probably correct. I started mentally sketching some version where we allow multiple ongoing navigate events, so that developers could get success signals for both `pushState()`s in the OP. But it quickly became nightmareish. Ultimately, the navigation API asks the web developer to buy into a paradigm where there is only one navigation ongoing at a time, and overlapping ones are treated as errors.

It's true that some of those "errors" (like SDN-then-SDN or XDN-then-SDN) result in two history entries, and some (like XDN-then-XDN) only result in one. But that's just a reflection of the fact that [browsers' existing handling of overlapping navigations and traversals](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/6927#issuecomment-987747199) is very complicated. And it's further evidence that developers should really prefer queuing up navigations, using `await navigation.navigate(...).finished`, to avoid this complexity.

----

Regarding @smaug----'s case,

```js
navigation.onnavigate = () => {};
navigation.onnavigateerror = e => {
  if (e.destination.url.endsWith("#1") {
    history.pushState(1, null, "#3");
  }
};
history.pushState(1, null, "#1");
history.pushState(1, null, "#2");
```

I can't tell what the full event sequence @natechapin is proposing with the early-exit fix is. I _think_ a reasonable sequence would be:

- `navigate` to `#1`,
- `navigateerror` to `#1`
- `navigate` to `#3`
- `navigateerror` to `#3`
- `navigate` to `#2`
- `navigatesuccess` to `#2`

with the intuition being that you always fire `navigateerror` on the navigation that's getting aborted before you fire `navigate` for the navigation that's replacing it.

But this stuff is stupid-complicated and I'm willing to be convinced of other ideas that make our lives simpler. Because as I said above, overlapping navigations are just not the happy path.

I realised one thing. In this case we have a call to `pushState`, requiring [#inform-the-navigation-api-about-aborting-navigation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#inform-the-navigation-api-about-aborting-navigation) to be called to ensure [#ongoing-navigate-event](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#ongoing-navigate-event) is `null`. But we have non-sync callers as well, and we really want the assertion to mean something there. So maybe the call to [#inform-the-navigation-api-about-aborting-navigation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#inform-the-navigation-api-about-aborting-navigation) should really happen in [#fire-a-push/replace/reload-navigate-event](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#fire-a-push/replace/reload-navigate-event) before calling [#inner-navigate-event-firing-algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#inner-navigate-event-firing-algorithm)

I've been playing around a bit with this and I have the following suggestion:

* Since this is an issue only for synchronous navigations (i.e the things that go through [#shared-history-push/replace-state-steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#shared-history-push/replace-state-steps)) we should add the fix to the spec for that and that only
* We add an optional boolean `isSynchronousNavigation` to [#fire-a-push/replace/reload-navigate-event](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#fire-a-push/replace/reload-navigate-event) that is default `false`
* We make [#shared-history-push/replace-state-steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#shared-history-push/replace-state-steps) call [#fire-a-push/replace/reload-navigate-event](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#fire-a-push/replace/reload-navigate-event) with `isSynchronousNavigation` set to `true`
* We make the first step of [#fire-a-push/replace/reload-navigate-event](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#fire-a-push/replace/reload-navigate-event) be:
1. If _isSynchronousNavigation_ is true then while _navigation_'s **ongoing navigate event** is not null:
1.1. <ins>abort the ongoing navigation</ins> given _navigation_

Given this we get 

* `navigate` to `#1`,
* `navigateerror` to `#1`
* `navigate` to `#3` 
* `navigateerror` to `#3`
* `navigate` to `#2`
* `navigatesuccess` to `#2`

as expected, and we get to keep the assert that the ongoing navigate event in [#inner-navigate-event-firing-algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#inner-navigate-event-firing-algorithm) should be null. I haven't checked Blink, but I wouldn't be surprised if this would work there as well, removing their crash.

@farre thanks so much for your suggested fix. I really appreciate you wading into this complexity and coming up with a concrete suggestion. I'm happy to write up a spec PR for it, and it sounds like we have web platform tests for most cases already. (Although maybe we should write one up for the Chrome crash case too.)

But I just wanted to double-check first: 

> * Since this is an issue only for synchronous navigations (i.e the things that go through [#shared-history-push/replace-state-steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#shared-history-push/replace-state-steps)) we should add the fix to the spec for that and that only

I think we also would pass this boolean for the fragment navigation case, right? Fragment navigations and pushState/replaceState navigations seem very similar to me in this regard.

I'm happy to be able to help improve things! And it's very convenient to do it while we're implementing it in gecko and navigation is what I'm thinking about the most. 

If you'd help me with a PR I'd be super happy, and I think you're correct that fragment navigation should also do this.

These are the [tests](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1974199) I'm planning to land.
